stack.title: Architecture & Stack
stack.tagline: How this site is built, why these technical choices, and what I learned along the way.

frontend.title: Frontend — React SPA
frontend.desc: React 19 + Vite app with animations, dark/light mode, full-screen snap scroll on home, FR/EN i18n, dynamic Open Graph SEO.

backend.title: Backend — REST API MVC
backend.desc: Node 20 + Express 5 in MVC architecture. JWT auth, rate limiting, input validation, strict CORS, asyncHandler everywhere, Helmet + CSP.

external.title: External services
external.desc: Anthropic Claude to generate articles. GitHub API for heatmap and dynamic skills. Hyperliquid for live trading positions. Make.com to publish on LinkedIn.

infra.title: Infrastructure & Deploy
infra.desc: Hosted on Fly.io Paris region. Multi-stage Docker, non-root user. MongoDB Atlas (2 clusters). GitHub Actions CI/CD auto-deploy on every main push.

diagram.visitorTip: A recruiter, a client, or yourself landing on gcn-data.fr.
diagram.flyTip: Single Docker container on Fly.io serving both the built frontend AND the Express backend. Multi-stage build: 1 image, 2 roles.
diagram.frontendTip: React 19 + Vite + Tailwind v4. SPA with client routing, FR/EN i18n, dynamic SEO via react-helmet-async.
diagram.backendTip: Express 5 in MVC. JWT auth, rate limiting (10 logins/15min), validation, strict CORS, Helmet + CSP, SIGTERM graceful shutdown.
diagram.mongoTip: 2 Atlas clusters: main (users, articles, projects, page views, AI usage) + bot (trades, signals, OHLC from Hyperliquid V8 bot).
diagram.claudeTip: Claude Sonnet 4.5 via official SDK. Hard-limit budget guard ($4.17/mo, $50/yr). Article generation from project context + GitHub activity.
diagram.githubTip: GitHub API for: contribution heatmap, dynamic skills (languages + dependencies), semi-auto project import to DB.
diagram.hyperTip: Hyperliquid DEX API for fetching open positions and live PnL on the dashboard's Trades widget.
diagram.makeTip: Generic webhook → Make.com → LinkedIn. Chosen to avoid the direct LinkedIn API (mandatory weeks-long review). n8n self-host migration planned.
diagram.linkedinTip: Auto-publish on every published article. Post includes title, excerpt, link and tags. Anti-duplicate handled by LinkedIn itself.

mongo.title: MongoDB rather than PostgreSQL
mongo.reasoning:
Flexible schemas: project highlights are arrays of strings, articles have free-form markdown, AIUsage tracks an evolving format. No SQL migration on every field add.

A personal portfolio's traffic doesn't justify a relational database's rigor.
mongo.tradeoff: No real joins — I use denormalization (e.g. articles.author is just an ObjectId, I populate on demand). Acceptable at my scale.

flyio.title: Fly.io rather than Vercel or Render
flyio.reasoning:
One deployment unit (frontend + backend in same container) instead of splitting front on Vercel and API on Render. fly.toml versioned.

Low latency for European visitors (cdg region). Auto-stop saves resources when site is idle.
flyio.tradeoff: 2-5s cold start after inactivity. Acceptable for a portfolio (a recruiter will wait). If traffic grows, I'll set min_machines_running=1.

webhook.title: Make.com rather than direct LinkedIn API
webhook.reasoning:
The official LinkedIn API requires an app review (2-8 weeks, often rejected for personal portfolios) and no longer supports posting from a personal profile without a Company Page.

Make.com handles the LinkedIn OAuth on its side. 5-minute setup, free up to 1000 ops/month.
webhook.tradeoff: Third-party service dependency. Mitigated by a generic payload: migrating to self-hosted n8n = just change one env var, zero refactor.

analytics.title: Custom analytics rather than Plausible/Umami
analytics.choice: Build it yourself in the dashboard
analytics.reasoning:
Consistent with the 'everything in my cockpit' philosophy. No external dependency, free forever, and a great exercise to understand how production tracking actually works.

Useful portfolio metrics (views, countries, sources, top articles) are also the simplest to implement — ~90% of a pro tool's value for 4-6h of code.
analytics.tradeoff: No click heatmap, no session replay, no A/B testing. Not relevant for a portfolio. If needed someday: add Microsoft Clarity in 1 line.

webhookGeneric.title: Generic webhook vs LinkedIn SDK
webhookGeneric.reasoning:
The SocialPublisher service sends a `{ platform, text, article: {...} }` JSON to a webhook. Zero coupling with Make, X, or LinkedIn in the code.

Tomorrow, when I have my own server, I migrate to self-hosted n8n by just changing the LINKEDIN_WEBHOOK_URL env var.
webhookGeneric.tradeoff: More logic in Make.com (final formatting per platform) than in code. Acceptable since Make is versionable.

snapscroll.title: Full-screen snap scroll on home
snapscroll.reasoning:
Immediately differentiates the site from a classic portfolio. Forces designing each section as a complete visual unit.

Matrix identity + accent glow = a visitor knows in 2 seconds it's a dev who loves what they do.
snapscroll.tradeoff: Less content visible at once vs a classic long scroll. Mitigated by limiting home to essentials (Hero, About, Skills, 6 projects, Contact) and putting details on /projects and /blog pages.

lessons.label: Lesson
lessons.1: Code is only 30% of the job. Every feature confronted me with problems that only appear on a production site: DNS, CORS behind proxy, LinkedIn anti-spam, Google cache, dotenv overridden by another app... That's what made me progress fastest.
lessons.2: The 'graceful degradation' pattern saves lives. External services (Anthropic, GitHub, Make.com) can fail. Every call has a fallback, every webhook a graceful skip if not configured. The site stays functional even when the ecosystem wobbles.
lessons.3: Building your own tracking is underrated. I have everything in my dashboard: analytics, AI budget, GitHub stats, live trading, articles. A single cockpit, not 5 open tabs. This unification is what makes the project alive in my eyes.
lessons.4: What isn't measured doesn't exist. Before analytics, I had no idea if anyone visited the site. Before the AI budget guard, I had no idea how many tokens I was consuming. Data transforms intuition into decisions.
